questions.cardText:
[Psychology] Which of the following best describes the “Dualism” perspective?
A. The personality is influenced by genes and the environment
B. Mind and matter are different
C. Emotions and rational thoughts are controlled by different parts of the brain
Answer: B. The psychological study of mind and matter originated from centuries of philosophical debate about the nature of consciousness and its relationship to the material world.
questions.de: Wie heißt die eng mit René Descartes verbundene Auffassung, dass Geist und Materie (bzw. Geist und Körper) grundverschieden sind?
questions.en: What name is given to the view, closely associated with René Descartes, that mind and matter (or mind and body) are fundamentally distinct?

timeline.labelEn: René Descartes publishes his Meditations, the classic statement of mind–body dualism
timeline.labelDe: René Descartes veröffentlicht seine Meditationen, die klassische Darlegung des Leib-Seele-Dualismus

questions.notes: A 'which best describes' question turned around: the description (mind and matter are distinct) is the clue, the term is the answer. Confirmed: dualism holds that mind and body are distinct and separable; associated with Descartes (1641).

questions.cardText:
[Political Science] “Realpolitik” refers to politics based on:
A. Ideals
B. Practical rather than moral or ideological considerations
C. Democracy
Answer: B.
questions.de: Welcher deutsche Begriff bezeichnet eine Politik und Diplomatie, die sich an praktischen Gegebenheiten statt an moralischen oder ideologischen Grundsätzen orientiert?
questions.en: What German term names an approach to politics and diplomacy based on practical circumstances rather than moral or ideological premises?

timeline.labelEn: Ludwig von Rochau coins the term in his Grundsätze der Realpolitik
timeline.labelDe: Ludwig von Rochau prägt den Begriff in seinen „Grundsätzen der Realpolitik“

questions.notes: Confirmed: Realpolitik is policy based primarily on given circumstances and factors rather than ideological, moral or ethical premises. Coined by Ludwig von Rochau (book of 1853, per his Wikipedia article).
